cr_data.provenance:
Anita O'Keeffe Young (1891‑1985), the artist's sister, Newport, Rhode Island, by 1970 [1]; returned to the artist's collection [2]; The Georgia O'Keeffe Estate,1986; bequest to Philadelphia Museum of Art, 1987 
1. Younger sister of Georgia O'Keeffe. Married to Robert Ralph Young (1897‑1958). 
2. The painting likely transferred back to the artist collection with her sister Anita's death in 1985 
(Source: Philadelphia Museum of Art, 2025)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Exam. at Amer. Place, March 1946. . . . No signature." Abiquiú Notebooks notes inscriptions 1, 2. Pictured in 1934 New York (An American Place) Stieglitz installation photograph, see Appendix III, figure 56. Reproduced in *Creative Art* (January 1928); reproduced and titled *Birch and Pine* in *Newark Evening News* (March 1934). Anita O'Keeffe Young was the artist's sister. She purchased many O'Keeffe pictures, and frequently traded those she had purchased for others. This may be an example of such a trade. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

credit_line: Bequest of Georgia O'Keeffe for the Alfred Stieglitz Collection, 1987
description: Three smooth branches of a white birch emerge from the bottom center of the work. The branches intertwine with green boughs from a pine tree that stands just behind the birch. The background of the composition is dark blue and black, with a glowing white light at the center.
imageCaption: Courtesy of Philadelphia Museum of Art.
